Responsive foundation

Breakpoints

FDS starts compact and treats 1024 × 768 as the required desktop baseline. These min-width references coordinate page composition; wider screens add breathing room, not essential functionality.

{breakpointGuidance.map(({name, value, pixels, reference, use}) => )}
BreakpointStarts atLayout intent
{name}{reference} {value} ({pixels}px) {use}

Use a component or container-specific breakpoint when its own content breaks before or after one of these viewport thresholds.

Width behavior on large screens

ContentMaximumBehavior
Forms
--fds-size-container-form		48remRemain aligned to the page grid; inputs do not stretch across the viewport.
Reading
--fds-size-container-reading		72chKeep paragraphs and guidance at a readable line length.
Standard pages
--fds-size-container-page		80remKeep page regions related while the shell and background continue to fill the viewport.
Data workspacesFluidUse available width for tables and operational canvases; constrain their internal columns instead.

How to apply the scale

  • Build the base layout first.Preserve the task, reading order, and primary action before adding columns.
  • Change layout when content needs it.Do not target a device name or add a breakpoint only to match the scale.
  • Keep 1024 × 768 complete.Dense freight workflows must remain usable without page-level horizontal scrolling.
  • Treat 1280px and above as enhancement.Add context or space; do not hide required controls below it.

components-actions-actiongroup--docs.content:
import {Canvas, Controls, Meta} from '@storybook/addon-docs/blocks';
import * as ActionGroupStories from './ActionGroup.stories';

<Meta of={ActionGroupStories} />

# ActionGroup

ActionGroup arranges related, independent actions with consistent spacing, wrapping, and alignment. It is a layout composition, not a single composite control.

## Action order

Place supporting actions first and the primary action last. Use no more than one primary action in a group.

<Canvas of={ActionGroupStories.SupportingThenPrimary} />
<Controls of={ActionGroupStories.SupportingThenPrimary} />

## Alignment

End alignment is the default for confirmation and page-level actions. Use start alignment where actions follow content or form fields in reading order.

<Canvas of={ActionGroupStories.StartAligned} />

## Mixed actions

Mix labeled and icon-only actions only when their relationship and the icon meaning remain clear. Prefer labeled buttons for unfamiliar or consequential actions.

<Canvas of={ActionGroupStories.MixedActions} />

## Wrapping

The group wraps without changing DOM or keyboard order. Verify that the visual order still reads from supporting to primary at the narrowest supported width.

<Canvas of={ActionGroupStories.Wrapping} />

## Boundaries

- Use ActionGroup for related actions, not merely controls that happen to be close together.
- Use separate buttons because each action remains independently operable.
- Do not use ActionGroup for selection, tabs, a joined split button, or a menu; those require complete interaction contracts of their own.

components-actions-button--docs.name: Docs
components-actions-button--docs.title: Components/Actions/Button
components-actions-button--docs.content:
import {Canvas, Controls, Meta} from '@storybook/addon-docs/blocks';
import * as ButtonStories from './Button.stories';

<Meta of={ButtonStories} />

# Button

Buttons trigger actions. Use links for navigation, short verb-first labels, and one primary action per decision area.

## Playground

Use Controls to test the supported variant, size, loading, width, disabled, and label contract.

<Canvas of={ButtonStories.Playground} />
<Controls of={ButtonStories.Playground} />

## Variants

Use primary for the dominant action, secondary for supporting actions, tertiary for low-emphasis actions, and danger only for destructive confirmation.

<Canvas of={ButtonStories.Variants} />

## Full width

Use `fullWidth` only inside a constrained form or narrow responsive layout.

<Canvas of={ButtonStories.FullWidth} />

## Sizes

- **Small · 28px:** dense toolbars, filters, tables, and pagination.
- **Medium · 32px:** default forms and standalone actions.
- **Large · 40px:** prominent page-level actions.

Do not mix sizes inside one button group.

<Canvas of={ButtonStories.Sizes} />

## Icon placement

Use a leading icon to reinforce the action. Use a trailing icon when it communicates direction, disclosure, or the result of activating the button. Keep the visible label; use `IconButton` for icon-only actions.

<Canvas of={ButtonStories.IconPlacement} />

### Menu trigger

Use a trailing disclosure icon and `aria-haspopup="menu"` when a button opens an action menu. The menu implementation must own open state, arrow-key navigation, Escape, focus movement, and focus return; FDS does not yet expose a standalone action-menu component.

<Canvas of={ButtonStories.MenuTrigger} />

## Keyboard shortcut

A shortcut hint is optional, visual help. It does not register the shortcut. Show it only when the application has wired the command, and keep it out of the button's accessible name.

<Canvas of={ButtonStories.KeyboardShortcut} />

## Loading

Loading prevents repeat activation while preserving the visible label and keyboard focus. The spinner replaces the leading icon, the trailing icon when no leading icon exists, or occupies the leading slot when the button has no icon. Use `loadingAnnouncement` to announce specific progress without changing the label.

<Canvas of={ButtonStories.LoadingStates} />

## Disabled and focus

Use `disabled` when an action is unavailable. Use `aria-disabled` only when the control must remain focusable, and explain the reason nearby. Hover, active, and focus are interaction states; use Tab to verify the visible focus ring.

<Canvas of={ButtonStories.Disabled} />
<Canvas of={ButtonStories.KeyboardFocus} />

## Accessibility

- Use the native button for actions and a link for navigation.
- Write a short, specific, verb-first label.
- Keep focus visible and do not disable a loading button in a way that drops focus.
- A displayed shortcut must match a real keyboard command and must not replace the visible label.

components-actions-iconbutton--docs.title: Components/Actions/IconButton
components-actions-iconbutton--docs.content:
import {Canvas, Controls, Meta} from '@storybook/addon-docs/blocks';
import * as IconButtonStories from './IconButton.stories';

<Meta of={IconButtonStories} />

# IconButton

IconButton is a compact action for a familiar icon whose meaning remains clear without visible text. Prefer a labeled `Button` when the icon needs explanation.

## Playground

Use Controls to test the supported tone, size, loading, disabled, and accessible-name contract.

<Canvas of={IconButtonStories.Playground} />
<Controls of={IconButtonStories.Playground} />

## Tones

Use the same hierarchy as Button: primary for the one dominant action, secondary for supporting actions, tertiary for compact low-emphasis actions, and danger only when the destructive outcome is clear from context. The icon, accessible name, and surrounding context—not color alone—communicate the action.

<Canvas of={IconButtonStories.Tones} />

## Sizes

- **Small · 28px:** dense toolbars, tables, and pagination.
- **Medium · 32px:** default standalone and form-adjacent actions.
- **Large · 40px:** prominent or touch-oriented actions.

Do not mix sizes inside one action group.

<Canvas of={IconButtonStories.Sizes} />

## Loading

Loading replaces the icon with progress, blocks repeat activation, preserves focus and the accessible name, and announces `loadingAnnouncement`.

<Canvas of={IconButtonStories.Loading} />

## Disabled and focus

Use `disabled` when an action is unavailable. Use `aria-disabled` only when the control must remain focusable, and explain the reason nearby. Hover, active, and focus are interaction states; use Tab to verify the visible focus ring.

<Canvas of={IconButtonStories.Disabled} />
<Canvas of={IconButtonStories.KeyboardFocus} />

## Accessibility

- Supply either `aria-label` or `aria-labelledby`; the icon itself is decorative.
- Use a recognizable icon whose visual meaning matches the accessible name.
- Prefer visible text when the action is unfamiliar, ambiguous, or consequential.
- Do not rely on tone alone to distinguish adjacent actions.

components-overlays-dialog--docs.name: Docs
components-overlays-dialog--docs.title: Components/Overlays/Dialog
components-overlays-dialog--docs.content:
import {Canvas, Meta} from '@storybook/addon-docs/blocks';
import * as DialogStories from './Dialog.stories';

<Meta of={DialogStories} />

# Dialog

Dialog presents one short, focused task above the current page. Use a page when the content needs navigation, multiple sections, or a durable URL.

## Context

Use a concise visible title. Add a description only when it helps the user decide or act.

<Canvas of={DialogStories.TitleAndDescription} />

## Actions

Place supporting actions before one primary action. Use `role="alertdialog"` only for an urgent confirmation that needs immediate attention; a danger button alone does not require it.
For destructive confirmations, place the safest enabled action first; an `alertdialog` moves initial focus there.

<Canvas of={DialogStories.ConfirmationActions} />
<Canvas of={DialogStories.DestructiveConfirmation} />

## Dismissal and focus

The native modal keeps focus inside, focuses the first control, closes with Escape or the visible close button, and returns focus to the trigger. Backdrop dismissal is on by default; set `dismissOnBackdrop={false}` when an outside click could discard unsaved work.

<Canvas of={DialogStories.KeyboardCloseAndFocusRestore} />

## Accessibility

- Keep the title visible and specific.
- Keep a visible close control even when footer actions are present.
- Put live status messages inside the dialog while it is open.
- Verify Tab and Shift+Tab remain inside and Escape returns focus to the trigger.

components-overlays-drawer--docs.name: Docs
components-overlays-drawer--docs.title: Components/Overlays/Drawer
components-overlays-drawer--docs.content:
import {Canvas, Meta} from '@storybook/addon-docs/blocks';
import * as DrawerStories from './Drawer.stories';

<Meta of={DrawerStories} />

# Drawer

Drawer is a modal right-side sheet for a quick preview, configuration, or bounded operational edit while preserving page context. Use a page for long or multi-step work.

## Default

The drawer is 540px wide on regular viewports, anchored to the right edge, and modal over the complete application surface.

<Canvas of={DrawerStories.DefaultRightSideDrawer} />

## Forms and unsaved work

Use a drawer only for a short, single-column form. Set `dismissOnBackdrop={false}` whenever an outside click could discard edits; Cancel and the close button remain explicit exits.

<Canvas of={DrawerStories.FormContent} />

## Overflow

Only the body scrolls when content exceeds the viewport; the title, close control, and actions remain available.

<Canvas of={DrawerStories.LongScrollableContent} />

## Responsive placement

At 768px and below, the drawer becomes edge-to-edge. At larger widths it remains right-aligned and leaves the dimmed page visible as context.
Use the Storybook viewport toolbar on the Default story to inspect both boundaries.

## Keyboard and focus

Drawer uses the same native modal contract as Dialog: focus moves inside, Tab remains contained, Escape closes, and focus returns to the trigger.

<Canvas of={DrawerStories.KeyboardCloseAndFocusRestore} />
